question.text: How many New World screwworm cases will be confirmed in Mexico in total before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the total number of animal cases of New World screwworm in Mexico before July 1, 2027, according to the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) [Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service current status report](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/current-status?page=1), rounded to the nearest 500.
question.fine_print:
The map and list of cases is updated on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 5:00 p.m. ET by the USDA. This question will resolve as the total number of animal cases on the latest report before July 1, 2027, provided this is published at the earliest by June 1, 2027.

If the USDA ceases reporting or significantly changes its criteria such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question will be **annulled**.

# Mexico New World screwworm (NWS) cases before July 2027: research notes

I found no data showing the question is settled. My best estimate is that Mexico's cumulative total stood at about 52,600 on 2026-11-17, about 22,000 more than the April figure quoted in the question. It is still growing by roughly 100 to 160 cases a day. A caveat: I could not read the USDA figure directly, so the totals below come from SENASICA (Mexico's animal health agency) as reported in the press.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-19: The APHIS current-status page returned a 403 error to the raw fetch. Through WebFetch, the Mexico map only showed "Loading..." because it is built by scripts, so no count was readable. The page was last modified 2026-11-18. It says the map updates Tuesdays and Thursdays at 5pm ET, and it points to SENASICA for figures. [APHIS](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/current-status?page=1)
- The USDA figure appears to track SENASICA's cumulative count, which runs from 2024-11-20. USDA's 20,591 on 2026-04-15 sits between SENASICA's 18,573 (2026-03-23) and "more than 22,000" (2026-04-26). [La Razón via search](https://www.razon.com.mx/mexico/2026/03/17/gusano-barrenador-aumentan-casos-y-altas-temperaturas-afectan-su-combate/)
- 2026-11-17: SENASICA reported 52,573 cumulative cases and 1,570 active, with the national count rising by "more than 100 a day". [Periódico Correo](https://periodicocorreo.com.mx/vida-publica/2026/nov/17/caen-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-en-guanajuato-a-35-la-cifra-mas-baja-en-4-meses-171709.html)
- Mid-November 2026: Quadratín reported 1,625 active cases nationally. [Quadratín Morelos](https://morelos.quadratin.com.mx/extiende-gusano-barrenador-su-presencia-en-morelos-suma-608-casos/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. About 52,600 is already well above the 30,000 bottom of the question's range, and the count only goes up.
- The latest report before July 1, 2027 will probably be the one on Tuesday 2027-06-29. That is about 224 days after the last data point.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-18: Nuevo León confirmed its fifth case of 2026. [MVS](https://mvsnoticias.com/nuevo-leon/2026/11/18/nuevo-leon-suma-quinto-caso-de-gusano-barrenador-en-2026-753870.html)
- 2026-11-17: Guanajuato's active cases fell from 79 to 35 between Nov 6 and Nov 17. New cases there averaged 6.06 a day in October and 3.18 a day since Nov 6. [Correo](https://periodicocorreo.com.mx/vida-publica/2026/nov/17/caen-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-en-guanajuato-a-35-la-cifra-mas-baja-en-4-meses-171709.html)
- 2026-11-16/17: US cases reached 139 to 142 across Texas, New Mexico and Arizona, including a Tucson horse. [Source NM](https://sourcenm.com/2026/11/16/repub/new-world-screwworm-spreading-rapidly-across-southern-states/), [KJZZ](https://www.kjzz.org/science/2026-11-17/arizona-is-working-to-contain-new-world-screwworm-as-cases-rise)
- 2026-11-16: Chihuahua had 83 active cases as of Nov 15. [El Diario](https://www.eldiariodechihuahua.mx/estado/2026/nov/16/registra-el-estado-83-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-858071.html)
- Late October 2026: Active cases were 1,958 at the end of October, and the cumulative count was 50,667. [Tierra Fuerte](https://www.tierrafuerte.mx/archivos/87212), [Segundo a Segundo](https://segundoasegundo.com/chihuahua-reporta-130-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-al-cierre-de-octubre/)
- 2026-10-22: SENASICA warned that ranchers in Campeche hide cases because they fear quarantines, so official counts may be too low. [PorEsto](https://www.poresto.com/campeche/2026/10/22/gusano-barrenador-campeche-ganaderos-ocultan-casos-temor-cuarentenas-advierte-senasica.html)
- October 2026: The Metapa sterile-fly plant in Chiapas opened on 2026-06-28 and is ramping toward about 100M flies a week by the end of 2026. Locals protested the smell. [Farm Progress](https://www.farmprogress.com/tv-and-radio/screwworm-fight-gets-a-new-weapon-the-smell-that-makes-it-work)

## 4. Base rates and trend

| 2026-01-07 | 13,335 | about 55 |

| 2026-04-15 (USDA) | 20,591 | about 88 |
| early June 2026 | 28,430 | about 157 |
| 2026-07-15 | 33,698 | about 128 |
| 2026-08-18 | 38,820 | about 151 |
| 2026-10-24 | 49,538 | about 160 |
| 2026-11-17 | 52,573 | about 126 |

Sources: [Yucatán](https://www.yucatan.com.mx/mexico/2025/12/05/ante-dificil-panorama-por-crisis-del-gusano-barrenador.html), [Excélsior](https://www.excelsior.com.mx/nacional/aumentan-68-casos-activos-barrenador-enero), [El Mundo](https://diario.elmundo.sv/el-mundo/mexico-confirma-500-casos-del-gusano-barrenador-en-una-semana), [Crónica](https://www.cronica.com.mx/nacional/2026/01/22/gusano-barrenador-suma-mas-de-14-mil-casos-en-mexico/), [La Razón](https://www.razon.com.mx/mexico/2026/06/05/avanza-gusano-barrenador-en-eu-primer-caso-aca-en-5-meses-200-mas/), [SENASICA PDF](https://dj.senasica.gob.mx/Contenido/files/2026/julio/AVANCE12-23072026_c7e9f5f9-9196-4618-bc34-f5c487f17ba9.pdf), [UnoTV](https://www.unotv.com/salud/gusano-barrenador-alcanza-30-estados-en-mexico-que-estados-no-registran-casos/), [ZOLO](https://www.zolonoticias.com/2026/10/26/chihuahua-reporta-133-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-del-ganado/).

- **Seasonality:** The series only goes back to November 2024, so there is just one comparable period.
  - From about Nov 19, 2025 (roughly 11,000, my estimate) to about Jun 30, 2026 (roughly 31,800, interpolated), about 21,000 cases were added.
  - Growth was slowest from December to February (55 to 67 a day) and picked up from April.
  - This year is running about 5 times higher in level than last year, and about twice as fast per day in the fall.
- **Simple arithmetic, not a forecast:** 224 days at the range of observed rates gives:
  - 55 a day: about 12,300 more, for a total of roughly 65,000
  - 95 a day (last year's Nov-to-Jun average): about 21,000 more, roughly 74,000
  - 150 a day: about 33,600 more, roughly 86,000
- **Caveat on the sources:** they disagree in places. Two cuts near Oct 24 gave 49,538 and 50,667, and late July cuts gave 34,698 and 35,142.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on cumulative Mexico cases.
- Related markets:
  - Polymarket "Screwworm National Emergency declared by Dec 31": 24.5% Yes.
  - Kalshi US human cases in 2026, "above 0": 17%.
- I found no expert or model projections of Mexico's cumulative count.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The northern hemisphere winter (December to February) slowed spread last year. The rate of new cases has already dipped in mid-November.
- Metapa output is ramping toward about 100M flies a week, on top of about 100M a week from Panama. Production numbers for November are unconfirmed.
- The US sterile-fly facility in Texas and the US response funding mentioned in news coverage (about $750M) could affect northern Mexico.
- Spring warming (March to June 2027) drove the sharp rise in 2026, from about 88 a day to about 157 a day.
- Reporting risks: under-reporting (as in Campeche), changes in how SENASICA or USDA count cases (which would annul the question), and whether the USDA map keeps updating.
- I did not find an official seasonal weather outlook tied to screwworm.

The latest is **52,573 cumulative animal cases as of 2026-11-17**. The question's own background figure (USDA, 20,591 through 2026-04-15) matches SENASICA's scale. That suggests both use the same running total since 2024-11-20, though I could not check this directly.

## 1. Resolution source

The raw fetch was blocked (HTTP 403). The page links to SENASICA's dashboard for Mexico figures, and the map updates Tuesdays and Thursdays at 5 p.m. ET. **Seasonality:** There is only one earlier season to compare against.
- Last year, from about 2025-11-20 to 2026-06-30, the count rose from 10,472 to about 31,000, an increase of roughly 20,500.
- Daily cases bottomed in winter at about 50 to 65 per day (December to March), then sped up from April to reach a peak of 150 to 165 per day in July and August.
- This year is running well above last year: active cases are 1,570 now against 924 a year ago, and the current pace (about 117 per day) is nearly double last November's (about 70 per day).
- From 2026-11-17 to 2027-06-30 is about 225 days. As simple arithmetic, not a forecast: 80 per day would end near 70,500, 117 per day near 78,900, and 150 per day near 86,300. Adding last season's increase of about 20,500 gives about 73,000.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Winter (December to February): last year this was when daily cases slowed the most. Watch whether the current pace drops toward 60 per day.
- The Metapa plant ramping up to 100 million flies per week by the end of 2026, which would roughly double sterile-fly supply alongside the Panama plant.
- Spring and summer 2027: last year, warming from April onward brought the fastest growth.
- Reporting quirks: last year the count barely moved over the holidays (about +300 from 2025-12-29 to 2026-01-08), and figures differ between outlets.
- The question is annulled if the USDA stops reporting or changes how it counts cases.
- I found no official seasonal weather outlook tied specifically to screwworm.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left: about 7.4 months. The deciding report is likely the USDA update on Tuesday 2027-06-29, about 224 days after the last data point.

(b) Latest known value: USDA reported 20,591 cumulative cases on 2026-04-15. The USDA page itself was unreadable when the research was done. SENASICA's cumulative count, which USDA appears to track, was 52,573 on 2026-11-17.

(c) If nothing changed: the total would be about 52,500. That is impossible in practice, because the count is cumulative and new cases are still being confirmed every day.

(d) If the current trend continued:
- At roughly 126 cases a day, the total would reach about 81,000.
- The pattern last year was a winter slowdown, roughly halving the rate from December to February, followed by a spring rise. Applying that shape gives:
  - December to February at about 90 to 110 a day.
  - March at about 120 a day.
  - April to June at about 150 to 180 a day.
- That adds about 26,000 to 29,000 cases, for roughly 78,000 to 81,000.
- Active cases have fallen from 1,958 at the end of October to about 1,570, and sterile-fly output from the new Metapa plant is ramping up. Both point slightly lower, so my median is about 77,500.

(e) Historical variation: daily rates over the past year ranged from 55 to 160 cases. Over 224 days that range implies 12,000 to 36,000 additional cases, so the total could plausibly land anywhere from about 65,000 to 88,000.

(f) Experts and markets: no market or expert projection covers Mexico's cumulative count. Related markets (a US national emergency declaration, US human cases) do not directly inform this number.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: sterile-fly releases double and a harsh winter suppresses the fly, so the rate falls to about 30 to 50 cases a day. Under-reporting also grows. The total would land near 60,000.
- High: spread across northern Mexico and a hot spring push the rate to 200 to 250 cases a day. The total would land near 100,000 to 110,000.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** About 110 to 130 new cases per day for 224 days gives a total of about 77,000 to 82,000. A seasonal model gives a similar result:
- Late November at about 110 per day.
- December to February at about 90 per day, a winter slowdown.
- March at about 110 per day.
- April to June at about 150 per day, a spring surge like 2026.

- Ramp-up of the Metapa sterile-fly plant.
- The spread advancing northward.
- Under-reporting.

(f) **Experts and markets:** I found no forecasts or markets on Mexico's cumulative count. The question creator's range is 30,000 to 100,000.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Metapa reaches full output plus a cold winter, and sterile-insect releases suppress the southern hotspots. Daily cases fall to about 40 to 50, and reporting fatigue or concealment grows, for a total of about 62,000.
- **High:** A mild winter keeps transmission going, and a spring surge to 200 or more per day hits as the fly spreads through the northern and central states. The total exceeds 100,000.
